newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Gencor unit comments on Colombia purchase.
newsitem.headline: Gencor unit comments on Colombia purchase.

text.p: South Africa's Gencor Ltd expressed satisfaction with its purchase of the Colombian government's 46.58 percent stake in the sprawling Cerro Matoso nickel mine Tuesday but declined to reveal further investment plans.

Gencor, through its subsidiary Billiton BVI Ltd, paid the base price of 178.4 billion pesos ($165.8 million) for the stake, made up of 5.38 million shares, said Clemente del Valle, a senior Finance Ministry official.
This is Gencor's second largest investment in Latin America.

Chris Pointon, manager of Gencor International Nickel Ltd, which already owned a controlling 52.3 percent stake in the mine, expressed satisfaction at the purchase but declined to reveal future investment plans.
"We're very satisfied. We have been a partner in the plant for the last 15 years. We're looking to the future with optimism," he said.
"After our operations in Brazil, Cerro Matoso is our next biggest investment in Latin America," he added.
Pointon said the mine produced 50 million pounds of nickel in 1996 and said he was hopeful output would be a "little higher" this year.
He declined to give specific details of investment plans but said there would be no change in the work force.
Billiton's was the only bid for the plant in an open auction conducted simultaneously through the country's three stock exchanges in Bogota, Medellin and Cali, Del Valle said.
The government sold 2.32 percent of its stake in the mine to Cerro Matoso employees on Dec. 16 for 4.17 billion pesos.

The auction by Colombia's Sociedad Fiduciaria Industrial S.A., a branch of the government's Industrial Development Institute, was managed by SBC Warburg Inc and Corfigan, a subsidiary of Colombia's Banco Ganadero
